question: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that 'This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**K C Wheare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• K C Wheare was a distinguished constitutional scholar known for his work on federalism and constitutional law.
 
• He praised the Indian Constitution's amending process for its variety and flexibility, which he considered wise and unique.
 
• Wheare emphasized that such variety in the amending process is rare among the world's constitutions.
 
• His observations highlight the robustness and adaptability of the Indian Constitution in accommodating changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Granville Austin**

 
 
• Granville Austin was an American historian who studied the Indian Constitution extensively.
 
• He is known for his seminal work, "The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation," which examines the making and functioning of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Austin's work is highly regarded for its in-depth analysis and insight into the Indian constitutional process.
 
 
 
• **Ivor Jennings**
 
 
• Sir Ivor Jennings was a British lawyer and academic who made significant contributions to the study of constitutional law.
 
• He was involved in the drafting of several constitutions in the Commonwealth countries, including India.
 
• Jennings emphasized the importance of conventions and practices in the functioning of a constitution.
 
 
 
• **HM Seervai**
 
 
• H.M. Seervai was a prominent Indian jurist and constitutional expert.
 
• He authored the influential book "Constitutional Law of India," which is a comprehensive commentary on the Indian Constitution.
 
• Seervai's work is widely cited in legal circles and has greatly contributed to the understanding of the Indian constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Amending Process in the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution provides a detailed procedure for its amendment in Part XX, Article 368.
 
• The amending process is categorized into three types: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with ratification by states.
 
• This flexibility allows the Constitution to be both rigid and flexible, accommodating necessary changes while maintaining stability.
 
• Amendments require different levels of parliamentary support and, in some cases, ratification by state legislatures, ensuring a broad consensus.
